        pid = ProjectId(patient_id)
        project = Project(
            project_id=pid,
            metadata=ProjectMetadata(
                project_id=pid,
                project_name=f"Caso {name}",
                patient_id=patient_id,
                patient_display_name=name,
                clinical_procedure="orthognathic",
                status=ProjectStatus.ACTIVE,
                created_at=_parse_br_date(created),
                updated_at=_parse_br_date(updated),
                last_opened_at=None,
                schema_version=1,
            ),
        )
        repository.create(project)


def main() -> int:
    app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    app.setStyle("Fusion")

    repository = InMemoryProjectRepository()
    _seed_projects(repository)
    catalog = ProjectCatalog(repository=repository)
    manager = ProjectManager(
        repository=repository,
        event_bus=EventBus(),
        access_policy=AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy(),
    )

    editor_registry = EditorRegistry()
    tool_registry = ToolRegistry()
    tool_registry.register("tool.log", LogTool)
    tool_registry.register("tool.toggle", ToggleTool)
    theme_service = ThemeService(theme=ThemeName.DARK)

    window = MainWindow(
        catalog=catalog,
        manager=manager,
        actor="debug",
        editor_registry=editor_registry,
        tool_registry=tool_registry,
        theme_service=theme_service,
    )

    window.home()._flow_list_widget().set_flows(
        [
            ("orthognathic_basic", "Cirurgia Ortognática"),
            ("orthognathic_advanced", "Cirurgia Ortognática Avançada"),
            ("facial_implants", "Implantes Faciais"),
        ]
    )

    # ----- Diagnostics (temporary) -----
    window.home().project_selected.connect(
        lambda pid: print(
            f"[selected] project={pid!r} current={window.home().selected_project_id()!r}"
        )
    )
    window.home().flow_selected.connect(
        lambda fid: print(
            f"[selected] flow={fid!r} current={window.home().selected_flow_id()!r}"
        )
    )

    _orig_set_ready = window.home()._start_button_widget().set_ready

    def _traced_set_ready(ready: bool) -> None:
        print(f"[start_button] set_ready({ready})")
        _orig_set_ready(ready)

    window.home()._start_button_widget().set_ready = _traced_set_ready

    window.show()
    return app.exec()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Debug script: launch the Workspace with a fake ModuleUISpec.

This script is a development tool. It is NOT part of production.

It builds a Workspace with:

- A fake EditorRegistry populated with DummyEditor instances.
- A ToolRegistry with LogTool and ToggleTool.
- A ThemeService (dark).
- A fake, coherent ProjectContext (ADR-0006 requires one).
- A ModuleUISpec that mirrors a typical clinical layout:
    LEFT     -> object_list
    CENTRAL  -> viewport_3d | (mpr_axial / mpr_sagittal)
    RIGHT    -> properties
    BOTTOM   -> console

The Workspace is created with ``debug_colors=True`` so that each
Area has a soft background color that makes its boundary visible:

    LEFT     -> soft blue
    CENTRAL  -> soft green
    RIGHT    -> soft yellow
    BOTTOM   -> soft lavender

The TopOverlay is registered automatically by the Workspace and
will be positioned over the Central Region. During debug it is

Run with:

    .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\debug_workspace.py

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QMainWindow

# ----- Project context ----------------------------------------------


def build_project_context() -> ProjectContext:
    """Build a fake, coherent ProjectContext for the debug Workspace.

    The Workspace never inspects the context beyond checking for its
    presence (see ADR-0006), but a coherent context keeps the debug
    run representative of production. All timestamps are timezone-aware
    UTC, as required by ProjectMetadata.
    """
    pid = ProjectId("p-debug")
    now = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
    return ProjectContext(

            project_id=pid,
            project_name="Debug Case",
            patient_id="pat-debug",

            clinical_procedure="orthognathic",

            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
            last_opened_at=None,
            schema_version=1,
        ),
        patient_summary=PatientSummary(
            patient_id=PatientId("pat-debug"),
            display_name="Debug Patient",
            birth_date=None,
            sex=PatientSex.MALE,
        ),
    )


# ----- Editor registry ----------------------------------------------


def build_editor_registry() -> EditorRegistry:
    """Register DummyEditor under several editor_ids.

    A single DummyEditor class is registered under several ids so
    that the LayoutBuilder can create independent instances for
    each slot. This mirrors the future reality where several
    concrete Editor classes will be registered under distinct ids.
    """
    registry = EditorRegistry()
    for editor_id in (
        "editor.viewport_3d",
        "editor.mpr_axial",
        "editor.mpr_sagittal",
        "editor.object_list",
        "editor.properties",
        "editor.console",
    ):
        registry.register(editor_id, DummyEditor)
    return registry


# ----- Tool registry ------------------------------------------------


def build_tool_registry() -> ToolRegistry:
    registry = ToolRegistry()
    registry.register("tool.log", LogTool)
    registry.register("tool.toggle", ToggleTool)
    return registry

def build_spec() -> ModuleUISpec:
    """Build a ModuleUISpec that mirrors the prototype layout."""
    return ModuleUISpec(
        areas=(
            AreaSpec(
                area_id="area.left",
                title="Lists",
                placement=Placement.LEFT,
                editor_layout=EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.object_list"),
            ),
            AreaSpec(
                area_id="area.central",
                title="Editing",
                placement=Placement.CENTRAL,
                editor_layout=EditorLayoutSpec.split(
                    SplitDirection.HORIZONTAL,
                    (
                        EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.viewport_3d"),
                        EditorLayoutSpec.split(
                            SplitDirection.VERTICAL,
                            (
                                EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.mpr_axial"),
                                EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.mpr_sagittal"),
                            ),
                        ),
                    ),
                ),
            ),
            AreaSpec(
                area_id="area.right",
                title="Tools",
                placement=Placement.RIGHT,
                editor_layout=EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.properties"),
            ),
            AreaSpec(
                area_id="area.bottom",
                title="Console",
                placement=Placement.BOTTOM,
                editor_layout=EditorLayoutSpec.leaf("editor.console"),
            ),
        ),
    )


# ----- Main ---------------------------------------------------------

    app.setStyle("Fusion")

======================================================================
FILE: scripts/seed_flows.py
======================================================================

"""Seed the flows root with example flow.json files.

Development tool. Not part of production.

Creates 3 flows under ``<flows_root>/<flow_id>/flow.json``:

- orthognathic_basic
- orthognathic_advanced
- facial_implants

Idempotent: if ``flow.json`` already exists for a flow, it is skipped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from cranioz.config.loader import ConfigurationLoader
from cranioz.infrastructure.app.app_path_resolver import AppPathResolver


def _step(step_id: str, module_id: str, flow_id: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "step_id": step_id,
        "name_key": f"flows.{flow_id}.steps.{step_id}",
        "module_id": module_id,
    }


def _build_flows() -> dict[str, dict]:
    basic_steps = [
        _step("organize_data", "patient", "orthognathic_basic"),
        _step("osteotomy", "osteotomies", "orthognathic_basic"),
        _step("guide", "orthognathic_guide", "orthognathic_basic"),
    ]
    advanced_steps = [
        _step("patient", "patient", "orthognathic_advanced"),
        _step("tomography", "tomography", "orthognathic_advanced"),
        _step("cephalometry", "cephalometry", "orthognathic_advanced"),
        _step("registration", "alignment", "orthognathic_advanced"),
        _step("osteotomy", "osteotomies", "orthognathic_advanced"),
    ]
    implants_steps = [
        _step("patient", "patient", "facial_implants"),
        _step("tomography", "tomography", "facial_implants"),
        _step("implants", "orthognathic_guide", "facial_implants"),
        _step("splint", "osteotomies", "facial_implants"),
    ]
    return {
        "orthognathic_basic": {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "flow_id": "orthognathic_basic",
            "name_key": "flows.orthognathic_basic.name",
            "version": 1,
            "steps": basic_steps,
        },
        "orthognathic_advanced": {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "flow_id": "orthognathic_advanced",
            "name_key": "flows.orthognathic_advanced.name",
            "version": 1,
            "steps": advanced_steps,
        },
        "facial_implants": {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "flow_id": "facial_implants",
            "name_key": "flows.facial_implants.name",
            "version": 1,
            "steps": implants_steps,
        },
    }


def _flows_root() -> Path:
    config = ConfigurationLoader().load()
    app_paths = AppPathResolver()
    app_paths.initialize(config.paths)
    return app_paths.flows_root


def main() -> int:
    root = _flows_root()
    print(f"Flows root: {root}")

    flows = _build_flows()
    created = 0
    skipped = 0
    for flow_id, data in flows.items():
        flow_dir = root / flow_id
        flow_file = flow_dir / "flow.json"
        if flow_file.is_file():
            print(f"  skip   {flow_id!r} - already exists")
            skipped += 1
            continue
        flow_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with flow_file.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(data, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            fh.write("\n")
        print(f"  create {flow_id!r}")
        created += 1

    print(f"\nDone. Created: {created}, skipped: {skipped}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Seed the filesystem repository with fake projects for manual testing.

This script is a development tool. It is NOT part of production.

It creates 5 fake projects in the CranioZ projects root, using the
same names as ``scripts/debug_home_page.py``. It is idempotent: a
project whose id already exists is skipped, so the script can be run
multiple times without error.

Run with:

    .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts\\seed_projects.py

After running, ``python -m cranioz`` will list these projects in the
Home Page's ProjectTable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from cranioz.application.event_bus import EventBus
from cranioz.application.project.project_access_policy import (
    AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy,
)
from cranioz.application.project.project_manager import ProjectManager
from cranioz.config.loader import ConfigurationLoader
from cranioz.domain.patient.value_objects.patient_id import PatientId
from cranioz.domain.project.project_id import ProjectId
from cranioz.infrastructure.app.app_path_resolver import AppPathResolver
from cranioz.infrastructure.project.filesystem_project_repository import (
    FilesystemProjectRepository,
)

# name, patient_id
_FAKE_PROJECTS = [
    ("Gabriel Silva", "12652"),
    ("Camila Souza", "52269"),
    ("Lucas Ferreira", "25892"),
    ("Beatriz Oliveira", "11286"),
    ("Rafael Santos", "21358"),
]

_SEED_ACTOR = "seed-script"


def _projects_root() -> Path:
    """Resolve the projects root using the same logic as the application."""
    config = ConfigurationLoader().load()
    app_paths = AppPathResolver()
    app_paths.initialize(config.paths)
    return app_paths.projects_root


def main() -> int:
    root = _projects_root()
    print(f"Projects root: {root}")

    repository = FilesystemProjectRepository(projects_root=root)
    manager = ProjectManager(
        repository=repository,
        event_bus=EventBus(),
        access_policy=AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy(),
    )

    created = 0
    skipped = 0
    for name, patient_id in _FAKE_PROJECTS:
        pid = ProjectId(patient_id)
        if repository.exists(pid):
            print(f"  skip   {name!r} ({patient_id}) — already exists")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        manager.create_project(
            _SEED_ACTOR,
            project_id=pid,
            project_name=f"Caso {name}",
            patient_id=PatientId(patient_id),
            patient_display_name=name,
            clinical_procedure="orthognathic",
        )
        print(f"  create {name!r} ({patient_id})")
        created += 1

    print(f"\nDone. Created: {created}, skipped: {skipped}.")
    if created:
        print("Restart the application to see the projects in the Home Page.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""CranioZ application entry point.

Boot sequence:
1. Load configuration.
2. Configure logging.
3. Create the QApplication.
4. Initialize application paths.
5. Initialize shared services (EventBus, CommandBus, TaskManager,
   TelemetrySink, ModuleRegistry).
6. Initialize the project subsystem.
7. Initialize the UI registries (editors, tools) and the theme service.
8. Create and show the MainWindow.
9. Start the Qt event loop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import getpass
import logging
import logging.config
from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QMessageBox

from cranioz import __version__
from cranioz.application.commands.in_memory_bus import InMemoryCommandBus
from cranioz.application.event_bus import EventBus
from cranioz.application.events import EventBusAdapter
from cranioz.application.flows.catalog import FlowCatalog
from cranioz.application.project.project_access_policy import (
    AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy,
)
from cranioz.application.project.project_catalog import ProjectCatalog
from cranioz.application.project.project_manager import ProjectManager
from cranioz.application.tasks.noop_task_manager import NoOpTaskManager
from cranioz.application.telemetry.noop_sink import NoOpTelemetrySink
from cranioz.config.loader import ConfigurationLoader
from cranioz.config.schema import Config
from cranioz.infrastructure.app.app_path_resolver import (
    AppPathInaccessible,
    AppPathResolver,
)
from cranioz.infrastructure.flows.filesystem_flow_repository import (
    FilesystemFlowRepository,
)
from cranioz.infrastructure.project.filesystem_project_repository import (
    FilesystemProjectRepository,
)
from cranioz.modules.builtin import BUILTIN_MANIFESTS
from cranioz.modules.registry.module_registry import InMemoryModuleRegistry
from cranioz.ui.editors.editor_registry import EditorRegistry
from cranioz.ui.main_window import MainWindow
from cranioz.ui.theme.service import ThemeName, ThemeService
from cranioz.ui.tools.builtin.log_tool import LogTool
from cranioz.ui.tools.builtin.toggle_tool import ToggleTool
from cranioz.ui.tools.registry.tool_registry import ToolRegistry

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_DEFAULT_LOGGING_CONFIG = Path(__file__).parent / "config" / "defaults" / "logging.yaml"


def _configure_logging(config: Config) -> None:
    if _DEFAULT_LOGGING_CONFIG.exists():
        with _DEFAULT_LOGGING_CONFIG.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            logging.config.dictConfig(yaml.safe_load(fh))
    logging.getLogger().setLevel(config.logging.level)


def _resolve_actor() -> str:
    try:
        return getpass.getuser()
    except Exception:
        return "local-user"


def _build_tool_registry() -> ToolRegistry:
    registry = ToolRegistry()
    registry.register("tool.log", LogTool)
    registry.register("tool.toggle", ToggleTool)
    return registry


def _build_theme_service(config: Config) -> ThemeService:
    try:
        theme_name = ThemeName(config.app.theme.lower())
    except ValueError:
        theme_name = ThemeName.DARK
        _logger.warning(
            "unknown theme %r; falling back to %s",
            config.app.theme,
            theme_name.value,
        )
    return ThemeService(theme=theme_name)


def main() -> int:
    config = ConfigurationLoader().load()
    _configure_logging(config)
    _logger.info("CranioZ %s starting", __version__)

    app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])

    # ----- Application paths -----------------------------------------
    app_paths = AppPathResolver()
    try:
        app_paths.initialize(config.paths)
    except AppPathInaccessible as exc:
        _logger.exception("cannot initialize application paths")
        QMessageBox.critical(
            None,
            "CranioZ cannot start",
            f"The application paths could not be initialized:\n\n{exc}",
        )
        return 1
    _logger.info("Projects root: %s", app_paths.projects_root)

    # ----- Shared services -------------------------------------------
    event_bus = EventBus()
    _logger.debug("Event bus initialized: %r", event_bus)

    command_bus = InMemoryCommandBus()
    _logger.debug("Command bus initialized: %r", command_bus)

    task_manager = NoOpTaskManager()
    telemetry = NoOpTelemetrySink()
    _logger.debug("TaskManager and TelemetrySink initialized (no-op)")

    event_bus_adapter = EventBusAdapter(event_bus)
    _logger.debug("EventBusAdapter initialized: %r", event_bus_adapter)

    module_registry = InMemoryModuleRegistry()
    for manifest in BUILTIN_MANIFESTS:
        module_registry.register(manifest)
    _logger.debug("ModuleRegistry initialized: %r", module_registry)

    # ----- Project subsystem -----------------------------------------
    repository = FilesystemProjectRepository(
        projects_root=app_paths.projects_root,
    )
    catalog = ProjectCatalog(repository=repository)
    manager = ProjectManager(
        repository=repository,
        event_bus=event_bus,
        access_policy=AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy(),
    )

    # ----- UI services ------------------------------------------------
    editor_registry = EditorRegistry()
    tool_registry = _build_tool_registry()
    theme_service = _build_theme_service(config)
    actor = _resolve_actor()

    # ----- Flows -------------------------------------------------------
    flow_repository = FilesystemFlowRepository(
        flows_root=app_paths.flows_root,
    )
    flow_catalog = FlowCatalog(repository=flow_repository)
    _logger.debug("FlowCatalog initialized: %r", flow_catalog)

    # ----- Main window ------------------------------------------------
    window = MainWindow(
        catalog=catalog,
        manager=manager,
        actor=actor,
        editor_registry=editor_registry,
        tool_registry=tool_registry,
        theme_service=theme_service,
        task_manager=task_manager,
        telemetry=telemetry,
        flow_catalog=flow_catalog,
    )
    window.show()

    _logger.info("Boot complete; MainWindow shown (actor=%r)", actor)
    return app.exec()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/event_bus.py
======================================================================

"""Application event bus.

Minimal synchronous publish/subscribe bus for application-level events.
Threading and async dispatch are out of scope for this phase.

Rules:
- Subscribers receive events synchronously, in registration order.
- Publishing an event with no subscribers is a no-op.
- A failing subscriber does not prevent other subscribers from running;
  errors are collected and re-raised after all subscribers have been
  notified.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any


class EventBusError(Exception):
    """Raised when subscriber dispatch fails."""


EventHandler = Callable[[Any], None]


class EventBus:
    """Synchronous in-process event bus."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._subscribers: dict[type, list[EventHandler]] = defaultdict(list)

    def subscribe(self, event_type: type, handler: EventHandler) -> None:
        """Register a handler for a specific event type."""
        self._subscribers[event_type].append(handler)

    def unsubscribe(self, event_type: type, handler: EventHandler) -> None:
        """Remove a previously registered handler.

        No-op if the handler is not registered.
        """
        handlers = self._subscribers.get(event_type)
        if not handlers:
            return
        try:
            handlers.remove(handler)
        except ValueError:
            return

    def publish(self, event: Any) -> None:
        """Publish an event to all handlers registered for its type.

        Dispatches in registration order. If any handler raises, the
        remaining handlers still run, and the collected exceptions are
        re-raised as an EventBusError at the end.
        """
        handlers = list(self._subscribers.get(type(event), ()))
        errors: list[BaseException] = []
        for handler in handlers:
            try:
                handler(event)
            except Exception as exc:
                errors.append(exc)
        if errors:
            raise EventBusError(
                f"{len(errors)} subscriber(s) failed while publishing {type(event).__name__}"
            ) from errors[0]

    def subscriber_count(self, event_type: type) -> int:
        """Return the number of handlers registered for an event type."""
        return len(self._subscribers.get(event_type, ()))

FILE: src/cranioz/application/commands/base.py
======================================================================

"""Base types for the Command mechanism (ADR-0007).

A Command is immutable data expressing an intent to change persistent
state. A CommandHandler validates, opens a transaction, mutates the
domain, commits, and publishes events. The CommandBus routes a Command
to its Handler by type.

This module defines the data and error types shared by every Command,
Handler, Bus, and Stack. It has no Qt, filesystem, or EventBus
dependency.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol, TypeVar, runtime_checkable

TCommand = TypeVar("TCommand", contravariant=True)
TResult = TypeVar("TResult", covariant=True)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Command:
    """An immutable intent to change persistent state."""

    command_id: str = field(default="")
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @classmethod
    def new(
        cls,
        *,
        command_id: str | None = None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> Command:
        """Return a new Command with a generated ``command_id``."""
        if command_id is None:
            command_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        if metadata is None:
            metadata = {}
        return cls(command_id=command_id, metadata=metadata, **kwargs)

    @staticmethod
    def new_id() -> str:
        """Return a fresh ``command_id``."""
        return str(uuid.uuid4())


@runtime_checkable
class CommandHandler(Protocol[TCommand, TResult]):
    """Executes a specific Command type."""

    def handle(self, command: TCommand) -> TResult: ...


# ----- Errors ------------------------------------------------------


class CommandError(Exception):
    """Base of all Command-related errors."""


class CommandNotRegistered(CommandError):
    """No Handler is registered for the given Command type."""


class CommandDispatchError(CommandError):
    """A Handler raised while dispatching a Command."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        command_id: str | None = None,
        command_type: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.command_id = command_id
        self.command_type = command_type
        super().__init__(message)

FILE: src/cranioz/application/commands/bus.py
======================================================================

"""CommandBus and CommandHandlerRegistry contracts (ADR-0007).

The Bus is the only entry point for state-changing operations. It
routes a Command to its Handler by type, calls the Handler
synchronously, and returns its result (or raises
``CommandDispatchError`` with the original exception as ``__cause__``).

The Bus does not validate. It does not open transactions. It does not
publish events. Those are the Handler's (or a future CommandExecutor's)
responsibility.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from cranioz.application.commands.base import Command, CommandHandler


@runtime_checkable
class CommandHandlerRegistry(Protocol):
    """Maps Command types to their Handler."""

    def register(
        self,
        command_type: type[Command],
        handler: CommandHandler[Any, Any],
    ) -> None: ...

    def resolve(
        self,
        command_type: type[Command],
    ) -> CommandHandler[Any, Any]: ...

    def contains(self, command_type: type[Command]) -> bool: ...

    def command_types(self) -> tuple[type[Command], ...]: ...


@runtime_checkable
class CommandBus(Protocol):
    """Routes Commands to their Handler."""

    def register(
        self,
        command_type: type[Command],
        handler: CommandHandler[Any, Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Register a Handler for the given Command type."""
        ...

    def unregister(self, command_type: type[Command]) -> None:
        """Remove the Handler for the given Command type.

        No-op if the type is unknown.
        """
        ...

    def dispatch(self, command: Command) -> Any: ...

    def can_dispatch(self, command_type: type[Command]) -> bool: ...



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/commands/in_memory_bus.py
======================================================================

"""InMemoryCommandBus — reference implementation of CommandBus.

Used by tests, by higher-layer contract tests, and by the early
bootstrap before the Application layer is fully wired. It registers
Handlers by Command type and dispatches synchronously on the caller's
thread.

Thread-safety: not thread-safe. Dispatch runs on the caller's thread.
The GUI thread is the expected caller.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from cranioz.application.commands.base import (
    Command,
    CommandDispatchError,
    CommandHandler,
    CommandNotRegistered,
)


class InMemoryCommandBus:
    """Reference implementation of ``CommandBus``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._handlers: dict[type[Command], CommandHandler[Any, Any]] = {}

    # ----- Registration ---------------------------------------------

    def register(
        self,
        command_type: type[Command],
        handler: CommandHandler[Any, Any],
    ) -> None:
        existing = self._handlers.get(command_type)
        if existing is handler:
            return
        if existing is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"a different handler is already registered for "
                f"{command_type.__name__}"
            )
        self._handlers[command_type] = handler

    def unregister(self, command_type: type[Command]) -> None:
        self._handlers.pop(command_type, None)

    # ----- Dispatch -------------------------------------------------

    def dispatch(self, command: Command) -> Any:
        handler = self._handlers.get(type(command))
        if handler is None:
            raise CommandNotRegistered(
                f"no handler registered for {type(command).__name__}"
            )
        try:
            return handler.handle(command)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise CommandDispatchError(
                f"handler for {type(command).__name__} raised "
                f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                command_id=command.command_id,
                command_type=type(command).__name__,
            ) from exc

    def can_dispatch(self, command_type: type[Command]) -> bool:
        return command_type in self._handlers

    # ----- Introspection --------------------------------------------

    def command_types(self) -> tuple[type[Command], ...]:
        return tuple(self._handlers.keys())

    # ----- Convenience ----------------------------------------------

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._handlers)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        types = [t.__name__ for t in self._handlers]
        return f"InMemoryCommandBus(handlers={types!r})"



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/commands/stack.py
======================================================================

"""CommandStack — undo/redo tracking (ADR-0007 §2.5).

The CommandStack does not execute Commands. It stores pairs
``(command, compensating)`` and returns the next Command to dispatch
on undo/redo. The caller (typically a future CommandExecutor) is
responsible for dispatching the returned Command on the CommandBus.

A Command with ``compensating=None`` is irreversible: ``undo`` pops it
and returns ``None``, which tells the caller that the Command cannot
be undone. Pushing any Command clears the redo branch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from cranioz.application.commands.base import Command


@runtime_checkable
class CommandStack(Protocol):
    """Tracks reversible Commands for undo/redo."""

    def push(
        self,
        command: Command,
        compensating: Command | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Record a dispatched Command and its compensating Command.

        ``compensating`` is ``None`` for irreversible Commands. In
        either case, ``push`` clears the redo branch.
        """
        ...

    def undo(self) -> Command | None:
        """Pop the last undoable Command and return its compensating.

        Returns ``None`` if there is nothing to undo, or if the popped
        Command is irreversible. The caller dispatches the returned
        Command when it is not ``None``.
        """
        ...

    def redo(self) -> Command | None:
        """Pop the last redone Command and return its original.

        Returns ``None`` if there is nothing to redo. The caller
        dispatches the returned Command.
        """
        ...

    def can_undo(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if there is at least one undoable Command."""
        ...

    def can_redo(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if there is at least one redone Command."""
        ...

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear both undo and redo stacks."""
        ...


class InMemoryCommandStack:
    """Reference implementation of ``CommandStack``.

    Two lists (undo and redo). Not thread-safe.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._undo: list[tuple[Command, Command | None]] = []
        self._redo: list[tuple[Command, Command | None]] = []

    def push(
        self,
        command: Command,
        compensating: Command | None,
    ) -> None:
        self._undo.append((command, compensating))
        self._redo.clear()

    def undo(self) -> Command | None:
        if not self._undo:
            return None
        command, compensating = self._undo.pop()
        self._redo.append((command, compensating))
        return compensating

    def redo(self) -> Command | None:
        if not self._redo:
            return None
        command, compensating = self._redo.pop()
        self._undo.append((command, compensating))
        return command

    def can_undo(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self._undo)

    def can_redo(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self._redo)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        self._undo.clear()
        self._redo.clear()

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._undo)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"InMemoryCommandStack(undo={len(self._undo)}, "
            f"redo={len(self._redo)})"
        )

======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/events/base.py
======================================================================

"""Base Protocols for the Events facade (ADR-0007, ADR-0012).

The ``EventBus`` in ``cranioz.application.event_bus`` is a synchronous
publish/subscribe mechanism. It has no concept of scope: a subscriber
is subscribed until it explicitly unsubscribes.

This module defines two facades over that bus:

- ``EventSubscription`` — scoped. Every ``subscribe`` returns a
  ``SubscriptionHandle``. ``dispose()`` cancels all handles created
  through this facade. The facade is idempotent after disposal.
- ``EventPublisher`` — publish-only. No ``subscribe``. Used where a
  component should emit events but must not observe others.

Neither facade raises from ``publish``: a handler that raises is
collected by the EventBus and re-raised as ``EventBusError``, which
the adapter logs and discards (fire-and-forget, ADR-0012 §2.2).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

EventHandler = Callable[[Any], None]


@runtime_checkable
class SubscriptionHandle(Protocol):
    """Handle returned by ``EventSubscription.subscribe``.

    ``cancel()`` removes the subscription. It is idempotent: calling it
    twice is a no-op. After ``cancel()``, the handler is no longer
    invoked.
    """

    def cancel(self) -> None: ...


@runtime_checkable
class EventSubscription(Protocol):
    """Scoped subscription facade over the EventBus.

    ``subscribe`` returns a handle. ``dispose`` cancels all outstanding
    handles created through this facade and prevents new
    subscriptions. After ``dispose``, ``subscribe`` raises
    ``SubscriptionClosed``.
    """

    def subscribe(
        self,
        event_type: type,
        handler: EventHandler,
    ) -> SubscriptionHandle: ...

    def dispose(self) -> None: ...


@runtime_checkable
class EventPublisher(Protocol):
    """Publish-only facade over the EventBus.

    The publisher can emit events but cannot subscribe. Used where a
    component should produce events without observing others.
    """

    def publish(self, event: Any) -> None: ...



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/events/bus_adapter.py
======================================================================

"""EventBusAdapter — scoped and publish-only facades over the EventBus.

The adapter wraps a ``cranioz.application.event_bus.EventBus`` (or any
object satisfying its structural shape) and exposes two Protocol
implementations. Each ``create_subscription()`` call returns a fresh
``EventSubscription`` with its own set of handles; disposing one does
not affect the others.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

from cranioz.application.events.base import SubscriptionHandle
from cranioz.application.events.errors import SubscriptionClosed

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

EventHandler = Callable[[Any], None]


class _SubscriptionHandle:
    """Handle for a single subscription."""

    __slots__ = ("_cancelled", "_event_bus", "_event_type", "_handler")

    def __init__(
        self,
        event_bus: Any,
        event_type: type,
        handler: EventHandler,
    ) -> None:
        self._event_bus = event_bus
        self._event_type = event_type
        self._handler = handler
        self._cancelled = False

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        if self._cancelled:
            return
        self._cancelled = True
        try:
            self._event_bus.unsubscribe(self._event_type, self._handler)
        except Exception:
            _logger.exception(
                "failed to unsubscribe handler %r from %r",
                self._handler,
                self._event_type,
            )


class EventBusAdapter:
    """Scoped and publish-only facades over a structural EventBus.

    The adapter does not own the bus. It borrows ``subscribe``,
    ``unsubscribe``, and ``publish``. It does not attempt to wrap
    handlers: the handler passed to ``subscribe`` is the handler
    invoked by the bus.
    """

    def __init__(self, event_bus: Any) -> None:
        self._event_bus = event_bus

    def create_subscription(self) -> _ScopedEventSubscription:
        """Return a fresh ``EventSubscription`` bound to this bus.

        Each call returns a new scope with its own handles. Disposing
        one scope does not affect the others.
        """
        return _ScopedEventSubscription(self._event_bus)

    def create_publisher(self) -> _EventBusPublisher:
        """Return an ``EventPublisher`` bound to this bus."""
        return _EventBusPublisher(self._event_bus)


class _ScopedEventSubscription:
    """``EventSubscription`` implementation backed by a single scope."""

    def __init__(self, event_bus: Any) -> None:
        self._event_bus = event_bus
        self._handles: list[_SubscriptionHandle] = []
        self._disposed = False

    def subscribe(
        self,
        event_type: type,
        handler: EventHandler,
    ) -> SubscriptionHandle:
        if self._disposed:
            raise SubscriptionClosed(
                "cannot subscribe on a disposed EventSubscription"
            )
        self._event_bus.subscribe(event_type, handler)
        handle = _SubscriptionHandle(self._event_bus, event_type, handler)
        self._handles.append(handle)
        return handle

    def dispose(self) -> None:
        if self._disposed:
            return
        self._disposed = True
        for handle in self._handles:
            handle.cancel()
        self._handles.clear()

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._handles)


class _EventBusPublisher:
    """``EventPublisher`` implementation backed by a single bus."""

    def __init__(self, event_bus: Any) -> None:
        self._event_bus = event_bus

    def publish(self, event: Any) -> None:
        try:
            self._event_bus.publish(event)
        except Exception:
            _logger.exception(
                "event publication failed for %r", type(event).__name__
            )

"""Errors for the Events facade."""

from __future__ import annotations


class EventFacadeError(Exception):
    """Base of all Events-facade errors."""


class SubscriptionClosed(EventFacadeError):
    """Raised by ``EventSubscription.subscribe`` after ``dispose``.

    Once a scope is disposed, no new subscriptions may be made through
    it. The caller must open a new scope.
    """


class EventPublicationError(EventFacadeError):
    """Raised by ``EventPublisher.publish`` when a subscriber fails.

    The underlying ``EventBus`` collects subscriber exceptions and
    re-raises an ``EventBusError``. The adapter logs it and discards it
    (fire-and-forget). This error is defined for callers that need to
    observe publication failures explicitly (e.g., a strict development
    adapter).
    """

FILE: src/cranioz/application/flows/catalog.py

"""FlowCatalog — read-only projection for the Home Page.

The catalog delegates every call to the repository. It does not cache.
It does not execute flows. It does not load step details until
``get_flow`` is called.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from cranioz.application.flows.definition import FlowDefinition
from cranioz.application.flows.repository import FlowRepository
from cranioz.application.flows.summary import FlowSummary


class FlowCatalog:
    """Read-only projection of flows known to a repository."""

    def __init__(self, repository: FlowRepository) -> None:
        self._repository = repository

    def list_flows(self) -> tuple[FlowSummary, ...]:
        return self._repository.list_summaries()

    def get_flow(self, flow_id: str) -> FlowDefinition:
        return self._repository.get(flow_id)

    def get_flow_summary(self, flow_id: str) -> FlowSummary | None:
        for summary in self._repository.list_summaries():
            if summary.flow_id == flow_id:
                return summary
        return None

    def search_flows(self, query: str) -> tuple[FlowSummary, ...]:
        normalized = query.strip().lower()
        all_summaries = self._repository.list_summaries()
        if not normalized:
            return all_summaries
        matches: list[FlowSummary] = []
        for summary in all_summaries:
            # Search by name_key (translated later by the UI).
            if normalized in summary.name_key.lower():
                matches.append(summary)
        return tuple(matches)

    def count(self) -> int:
        return len(self._repository.list_summaries())

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return len(self._repository.list_summaries()) == 0

    def contains(self, flow_id: str) -> bool:
        return self._repository.exists(flow_id)

    def list_definitions(self) -> tuple[FlowDefinition, ...]:
        """Return full definitions for all flows in the catalog.

        The repository is the source of truth. Corrupted flows are
        skipped by the repository's ``list_summaries``; a flow whose
        ``get`` raises during this call is propagated (the caller
        should prefer ``list_summaries`` when it only needs the
        projection).
        """
        return tuple(
            self._repository.get(summary.flow_id)
            for summary in self._repository.list_summaries()
        )

FILE: src/cranioz/application/flows/definition.py

"""FlowDefinition and FlowStep — declarative flow content."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlowStep:
    """One step of a clinical flow.

    Steps are ordered. ``module_id`` is the id of the Module that
    handles this step. ``name_key`` is a translation key for the
    user-facing label.
    """

    step_id: str
    name_key: str
    module_id: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.step_id:
            raise ValueError("FlowStep.step_id must not be empty")
        if not self.name_key:
            raise ValueError("FlowStep.name_key must not be empty")
        if not self.module_id:
            raise ValueError("FlowStep.module_id must not be empty")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlowDefinition:
    """A clinical flow, loaded from ``flow.json``."""

    flow_id: str
    name_key: str
    version: int
    steps: tuple[FlowStep, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.flow_id:
            raise ValueError("FlowDefinition.flow_id must not be empty")
        if not self.name_key:
            raise ValueError("FlowDefinition.name_key must not be empty")
        if self.version < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"FlowDefinition.version must be >= 1, got {self.version}"
            )
        if not self.steps:
            raise ValueError("FlowDefinition.steps must not be empty")
        ids = [s.step_id for s in self.steps]
        if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
            raise ValueError(
                "FlowDefinition.steps must have unique step_ids"
            )

    def step_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.steps)

FILE: src/cranioz/application/flows/in_memory_repository.py

"""InMemoryFlowRepository — reference implementation of FlowRepository."""

from __future__ import annotations

from cranioz.application.flows.definition import FlowDefinition
from cranioz.application.flows.errors import (
    FlowCorrupted,
    FlowNotFound,
)
from cranioz.application.flows.summary import FlowSummary


class InMemoryFlowRepository:
    """Reference implementation of ``FlowRepository``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._flows: dict[str, FlowDefinition] = {}
        self._corrupted: set[str] = set()

    def _mark_corrupted(self, flow_id: str) -> None:
        self._corrupted.add(flow_id)

    def add(self, flow: FlowDefinition) -> None:
        self._flows[flow.flow_id] = flow
        self._corrupted.discard(flow.flow_id)

    def list_summaries(self) -> tuple[FlowSummary, ...]:
        return tuple(
            FlowSummary.from_definition(f)
            for flow_id, f in self._flows.items()
            if flow_id not in self._corrupted
        )

    def list_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(self._flows.keys())

    def get(self, flow_id: str) -> FlowDefinition:
        if flow_id in self._corrupted:
            raise FlowCorrupted(
                f"flow is corrupted: {flow_id!r}", flow_id=flow_id
            )
        try:
            return self._flows[flow_id]
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise FlowNotFound(
                f"flow not found: {flow_id!r}", flow_id=flow_id
            ) from exc

    def exists(self, flow_id: str) -> bool:
        return flow_id in self._flows and flow_id not in self._corrupted

"""FlowSummary — lightweight read-only projection."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from cranioz.application.flows.definition import FlowDefinition


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FlowSummary:
    """Lightweight projection of a flow for the Home Page.

    Carries only what the ``FlowList`` needs to render a row: the flow
    id, the translation key for the display name, and the number of
    steps. Step details are loaded on demand.
    """

    flow_id: str
    name_key: str
    step_count: int

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.flow_id:
            raise ValueError("FlowSummary.flow_id must not be empty")
        if not self.name_key:
            raise ValueError("FlowSummary.name_key must not be empty")
        if self.step_count < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"FlowSummary.step_count must be >= 1, got {self.step_count}"
            )

    @classmethod
    def from_definition(cls, definition: FlowDefinition) -> FlowSummary:
        return cls(
            flow_id=definition.flow_id,
            name_key=definition.name_key,
            step_count=definition.step_count(),
        )

FILE: src/cranioz/application/project/in_memory_project_repository.py
======================================================================

"""InMemoryProjectRepository — reference implementation of ProjectRepository.

This implementation is the canonical reference for the contract defined
in `project_repository.py`. It is used by:

- Contract tests, which run the same suite against every implementation.
- Higher-layer tests (Project Manager, Project Catalog), where filesystem
  I/O would make tests slow and brittle.
- Early integration of the Home Page, before the filesystem adapter is
  available.

It is not a toy. It respects every documented failure mode of the
Protocol, including `ProjectAlreadyExists`, `ProjectNotFound`,
`ProjectCorrupted` (for previously-injected corrupted entries), and
`ProjectStorageError` (for explicitly-injected failure modes).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from cranioz.application.project.project_errors import (
    ProjectAlreadyExists,
    ProjectCorrupted,
    ProjectNotFound,
)
from cranioz.domain.project.project import Project
from cranioz.domain.project.project_id import ProjectId
from cranioz.domain.project.project_summary import ProjectSummary


class InMemoryProjectRepository:
    """Reference implementation of `ProjectRepository` backed by a dict.

    Not thread-safe. The Project Manager (Peça 7.5) is the only
    caller, and the application runs it on the main thread.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # Stores the full aggregate. Values are the *same* instances
        # the caller passed in `create` or `update`. This mirrors the
        # semantics of a filesystem repository: persistence does not
        # deep-copy, it stores the serialized representation; callers
        # that mutate the Project in place are responsible for calling
        # `update` to persist the mutation. Tests that need defensive
        # copying should copy explicitly.
        self._projects: dict[ProjectId, Project] = {}

        # Set of ids that should be reported as corrupted on `get`.
        # Used by tests to exercise the `ProjectCorrupted` path
        # without simulating a filesystem. Never populated by the
        # normal `create`/`update` path.
        self._corrupted: set[ProjectId] = set()

    # ----- Test support ---------------------------------------------

    def _mark_corrupted(self, project_id: ProjectId) -> None:
        """Mark a project as corrupted for testing purposes.

        After this call, `get` raises `ProjectCorrupted` for the given
        id, and `list_metadata` skips it. Used by contract tests to
        verify that a `ProjectCorrupted` does not crash `list_metadata`.
        """
        self._corrupted.add(project_id)

    # ----- ProjectRepository ----------------------------------------

    def create(self, project: Project) -> None:
        if project.project_id in self._projects:
            raise ProjectAlreadyExists(
                f"project already exists: {project.project_id.value!r}",
                project_id=project.project_id,
            )
        self._projects[project.project_id] = project

    def get(self, project_id: ProjectId) -> Project:
        if project_id in self._corrupted:
            raise ProjectCorrupted(
                f"project is corrupted: {project_id.value!r}",
                project_id=project_id,
            )
        try:
            return self._projects[project_id]
        except KeyError as exc:
            raise ProjectNotFound(
                f"project not found: {project_id.value!r}",
                project_id=project_id,
            ) from exc

    def update(self, project: Project) -> None:
        if project.project_id not in self._projects:
            raise ProjectNotFound(
                f"project not found: {project.project_id.value!r}",
                project_id=project.project_id,
            )
        self._projects[project.project_id] = project

    def delete(self, project_id: ProjectId) -> None:
        if project_id not in self._projects:
            raise ProjectNotFound(
                f"project not found: {project_id.value!r}",
                project_id=project_id,
            )
        del self._projects[project_id]
        # Corrupted markers become irrelevant once the id is deleted.
        self._corrupted.discard(project_id)

    def exists(self, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        return project_id in self._projects

    def list_metadata(self) -> tuple[ProjectSummary, ...]:
        summaries: list[ProjectSummary] = []
        for project_id, project in self._projects.items():
            if project_id in self._corrupted:
                continue
            summaries.append(ProjectSummary.from_metadata(project.metadata))
        return tuple(summaries)

    def list_ids(self) -> tuple[ProjectId, ...]:
        return tuple(self._projects.keys())

FILE: src/cranioz/application/project/project_access_policy.py
======================================================================

"""ProjectAccessPolicy — authorization contract for project lifecycle.

The policy answers "may this actor perform this operation on this
project?". It is evaluated at the Project Manager boundary
(project.md §15): the Manager consults the policy before mutating
state, never after.

Design rules (see `project.md` §15, §28):

- The policy is a Protocol. Concrete implementations may be
  permissive (single-user, development, first boot) or restrictive
  (institutional deployments, role-based access).
- The policy is **read-only**. It does not mutate state, does not
  publish events, does not access persistence. It receives an
  `Actor` and a `ProjectId` (or nothing, for `can_create`) and
  returns a boolean.
- An `Actor` is a string for now. It identifies who is performing
  the operation. In single-user mode (the initial deployment), the
  bootstrap passes a stable identifier (e.g. the OS username, or a
  configured professional id). When the application gains a proper
  user model, `Actor` will become a richer value object; the
  Protocol signature will not need to change for the common case.
- `AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy` is the initial implementation. It
  returns True for every operation. It exists so the Project
  Manager has a policy to consult from day one, and so tests can
  substitute a denying policy to verify the Manager's error paths.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from cranioz.domain.project.project_id import ProjectId

# An Actor identifies who is performing the operation. Kept as a
# string alias for now; the application has no user model yet.
# When a proper user model exists (roles, institutions), this alias
# becomes a class, and callers that already pass strings continue
# to work via a compatibility shim.
Actor = str


@runtime_checkable
class ProjectAccessPolicy(Protocol):
    """Authorization contract for project lifecycle operations."""

    def can_create(self, actor: Actor) -> bool:
        """Return True if `actor` may create a new project."""
        ...

    def can_open(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        """Return True if `actor` may open the given project."""
        ...

    def can_update(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        """Return True if `actor` may update the given project."""
        ...

    def can_delete(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        """Return True if `actor` may delete the given project."""
        ...


class AllowAllProjectAccessPolicy:
    """Permissive policy: every actor may do everything.

    This is the initial implementation for single-user deployments
    and for tests that do not care about authorization. It is a
    deliberate no-op, not a security boundary. A future
    RoleBasedProjectAccessPolicy will replace it for institutional
    deployments without changing the Project Manager's code.
    """

    def can_create(self, actor: Actor) -> bool:
        return True

    def can_open(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        return True

    def can_update(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        return True

    def can_delete(self, actor: Actor, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        return True



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/project/project_catalog.py
======================================================================

"""ProjectCatalog — read-only discovery projection.

The ProjectCatalog is the read model consumed by the Home Page
(project.md §5, §7; startup_project_opening_workflow.md §4). It answers
"which projects exist and what do they look like?" without loading
clinical data.

Design rules (see `project.md`):

- The catalog is **read-only**. It does not create, modify, delete,
  archive, or restore projects.
- The catalog is **not the source of truth**. It is a projection of
  what `ProjectRepository.list_metadata()` reports. If the repository
  changes, the next call to the catalog reflects the change; there is
  no cache to invalidate.
- The catalog **does not implement lifecycle policy**. It reports
  what exists. Whether a project is "openable", "in use", or
  "archived per policy" is the Project Manager's concern (piece 7.5).
- The catalog **does not maintain an independent authoritative list**.
  It has no `_projects` attribute. Every call delegates to the
  repository.
- The catalog **does not read from the filesystem or any other I/O**.
  It only consumes the repository, which already translates
  infrastructure failures into the `ProjectRepositoryError` family.

Why no cache in this piece:

The catalog will be called every time the Home Page refreshes. On a
local SSD, reading a few `project.json` files takes microseconds per
project. Premature caching would introduce invalidation bugs (stale
data after `ProjectDeleted`, cache misses during module switch) for
no measured benefit. If future profiling shows the catalog is a hot
path, a cache will be added in a separate piece, explicitly
invalidated by subscribing to `ProjectCreated` / `ProjectUpdated` /
`ProjectDeleted`. Until then: no cache.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from cranioz.application.project.project_repository import ProjectRepository
from cranioz.domain.project.project_id import ProjectId
from cranioz.domain.project.project_summary import ProjectSummary


class ProjectCatalog:
    """Read-only projection of the projects known to a repository.

    The catalog is the entry point for discovery: listing, searching,
    and looking up project summaries. It is not the entry point for
    lifecycle operations (create/open/close/delete); those belong to
    the Project Manager (piece 7.5).
    """

    def __init__(self, repository: ProjectRepository) -> None:
        self._repository = repository

    # ----- Listing ---------------------------------------------------

    def list_projects(self) -> tuple[ProjectSummary, ...]:
        """Return summaries of all projects known to the repository.

        Order is unspecified. Returns an empty tuple when no project
        exists (not an error). Propagates `ProjectStorageError` if the
        repository cannot list at all.
        """
        return self._repository.list_metadata()

    # ----- Lookup ----------------------------------------------------

    def get_project_summary(
        self,
        project_id: ProjectId,
    ) -> ProjectSummary | None:
        """Return the summary of a specific project, or None if unknown.

        The catalog does **not** raise `ProjectNotFound`. It returns
        `None`. Rationale: for discovery purposes, "not in the catalog"
        and "not persisted" are equivalent — the Home Page shows the
        same empty state either way. Callers that need to distinguish
        "not found" from "storage failure" should query the repository
        directly, or use `ProjectManager.get_project` (piece 7.5),
        which does raise.

        Propagates `ProjectStorageError` if the repository cannot list
        at all (as opposed to "the specific id is not present").
        """
        for summary in self._repository.list_metadata():
            if summary.project_id == project_id:
                return summary
        return None

    # ----- Search ----------------------------------------------------

    def search_projects(self, query: str) -> tuple[ProjectSummary, ...]:
        """Return summaries whose text fields match `query`.

        Matching is **case-insensitive substring** over:
        - `project_name`
        - `patient_display_name`

        No regex. No fuzzy matching. No ranking. `query` is treated as
        a literal substring, after `strip()`. An empty or
        whitespace-only query returns all projects (equivalent to
        `list_projects()`), which is the natural behavior for a
        search-as-you-type input.

        Rationale for no regex: the input comes from a user-facing
        search box. Allowing regex opens a ReDoS surface and is not
        what users expect from a "search" field. If advanced matching
        is ever needed, it will be an explicit `advanced_search`
        method with its own contract.

        Order is unspecified. Returns an empty tuple when nothing
        matches.
        """
        normalized = query.strip().lower()
        all_summaries = self._repository.list_metadata()
        if not normalized:
            return all_summaries

        matches: list[ProjectSummary] = []
        for summary in all_summaries:
            if (
                normalized in summary.project_name.lower()
                or normalized in summary.patient_display_name.lower()
            ):
                matches.append(summary)
        return tuple(matches)

    # ----- Convenience -----------------------------------------------

    def count(self) -> int:
        """Return the number of projects known to the repository."""
        return len(self._repository.list_metadata())

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if the repository reports no projects."""
        return len(self._repository.list_metadata()) == 0

    def contains(self, project_id: ProjectId) -> bool:
        """Return True if a project with the given id is discoverable.

        Cheap check; implemented via `get_project_summary`.
        """
        return self.get_project_summary(project_id) is not None



======================================================================
FILE: src/cranioz/application/project/project_context.py
======================================================================

"""ProjectContext — immutable initialization snapshot.

The ProjectContext is created when the Project Manager opens a
project (Peça 7.5). It is the runtime representation handed to the
Workspace: everything the Workspace needs to know about the active
project, and nothing more.

Design rules (see `project.md` §17, `startup_project_opening_workflow.md` §9):

- The context is **frozen**. The Workspace must never mutate it.
- The context is **not** the Project. It does not own the project's
  lifecycle; the Project Manager does. Discarding the context does not
  discard the project.
- The context carries **no service locator**. Services (ProjectManager,
  Repository, EventBus, ...) are injected via dependency injection by
  the bootstrap, not resolved through the context. The note in
  `project.md` §17 is explicit: the context is data, not a registry.
- The context carries **no physical paths**. Logical references only
  (`project_id`, `workflow_id`); physical path resolution belongs to
  `ProjectPathResolver` at the infrastructure boundary.
- `workflow_id` and `workflow_config` are optional. A project may be
  opened before a clinical workflow is selected
  (`startup_project_opening_workflow.md` §10: "If no flow is resolved,
  the Workspace opens in flow selection mode"). The two are either
  both set or both `None` — a workflow id without a config is
  meaningless.
- `object_references` is a tuple, not a list. Immutability is
  structural, not just by convention.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from cranioz.domain.patient.patient_summary import PatientSummary
from cranioz.domain.project.project_id import ProjectId
from cranioz.domain.project.project_metadata import ProjectMetadata


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ObjectReference:
    """A logical reference to a domain object visible to the Workspace.

    The context does not carry the object itself; it carries enough
    to *identify* it. Resolution to the live object happens through
    the Project's `DomainObjectStore` (see `scene.md` §4), which is
    not part of the context.
    """

    object_id: str
    kind: str
    display_name: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.object_id:
            raise ValueError("object_id must not be empty")
        if not self.kind:
            raise ValueError("kind must not be empty")
        if not self.display_name:
            raise ValueError("display_name must not be empty")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProjectContext:
    """Immutable snapshot handed to the Workspace when a project opens.

    Every field is a plain domain value. No service, no callable, no
    physical path. The Workspace consumes it; it does not mutate it and
    it does not fetch anything the context does not carry.
    """

    project_id: ProjectId
    metadata: ProjectMetadata
    patient_summary: PatientSummary
    workflow_id: str | None = None
    workflow_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    object_references: tuple[ObjectReference, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.metadata.project_id != self.project_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "metadata.project_id must match project_id "
                f"(metadata={self.metadata.project_id.value!r}, "
                f"context={self.project_id.value!r})"
            )

        if (self.workflow_id is None) != (self.workflow_config is None):
            raise ValueError(
                "workflow_id and workflow_config must be set together or both be None"
            )

    def has_workflow(self) -> bool:
        """Return True if a clinical workflow has been selected."""
        return self.workflow_id is not None

    def with_workflow(
        self,
        workflow_id: str,
        workflow_config: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> ProjectContext:
        """Return a new context with the workflow attached."""
        if not workflow_id:
            raise ValueError("workflow_id must not be empty")
        return ProjectContext(
            project_id=self.project_id,
            metadata=self.metadata,
            patient_summary=self.patient_summary,
            workflow_id=workflow_id,
            workflow_config=dict(workflow_config),
            object_references=self.object_references,
        )

    def with_object_references(
        self,
        object_references: tuple[ObjectReference, ...],
    ) -> ProjectContext:
        """Return a new context with different object references."""
        return ProjectContext(
            project_id=self.project_id,
            metadata=self.metadata,
            patient_summary=self.patient_summary,
            workflow_id=self.workflow_id,
            workflow_config=dict(self.workflow_config) if self.workflow_config else None,
            object_references=object_references,
        )
